S4Drive 0.2.0 treats folders as folders: renaming, moving or deleting one is a single change that reaches your other devices at once, however many files it holds. This release also fixes several cases where a rename could turn into a delete.

## ✨ New
- **Folders sync as folders**: renaming, moving or deleting a folder is one change instead of one per file, so even large folders move in seconds.
- **Empty folders sync** to your other devices.
- **One folder, not two**: the same folder created on two devices while offline merges into one when they reconnect.
- **Device names in conflict copies**: copies are named after the device that made them (`report (conflict from laptop …).md`). Set the name with `--device-name`; it defaults to the host name.
- **`--poll-interval` for `sync start`**: sets how often the CLI checks the bucket for changes from other devices (10 s by default, up to 10× longer while idle).

## 🛠 Improvements
- A moved folder is not re-read: files the device already knows are recognised by size and modification time.
- `metadata tree` shows full paths.
- `restore-bucket` puts files back under the latest names of their folders and leaves out files of deleted folders.
- A device that commits at the same moment as another one retries instead of reporting a conflict.

## 🐛 Fixes
- Renaming a folder no longer deletes its files and uploads them again, and renamed files no longer end up in the local trash.
- A folder moved into another folder on a second device no longer creates duplicates and conflict copies.
- Conflict copies no longer say "device" instead of the device name.
- A second device no longer stops syncing with "revision id already exists".
- A file deleted twice is no longer deleted again on every sync pass.

## ⬆️ Upgrading
- Update every device. The first 0.2.0 device that connects upgrades the bucket to metadata schema 2; after that, 0.1.x clients stop with "unsupported metadata schema version 2" instead of misreading your files.
- Your files stay where they are and nothing is uploaded again. The first time you rename a folder synced by 0.1.x, S4Drive updates each file inside it once; later renames are a single change.
